description: Routing claims copied from the 2026-09-26 rerun captures for public Cal.com PR10967. Source bodies, repository bindings, opaque graph IDs, and account metadata are excluded. Scripted grouping is an architecture check, not a model quality measurement.

investigations.question: Are the Prisma fields `Booking.destinationCalendar` and `User.destinationCalendar` still single objects (as in old code), or were they converted to arrays by this PR?
investigations.claim: If the model fields are now arrays, `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` produces a nested array (`[[...]]`), and the empty-array case `[]` is truthy, so the ternary would wrap an empty array as `[[]]`, breaking the calendar invite email.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: The Prisma schema / Booking and User model definitions for destinationCalendar (single optional relation vs array), which are not present in the supplied diff or related changes.

investigations.question: Was `sendOrganizerRequestReminderEmail` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:231-241) and its CalendarEvent consumer migrated to expect `destinationCalendar` as an array?
investigations.claim: This cron now passes an array where it previously passed a single object (or null); if the email sender still treats destinationCalendar as a single object (e.g., accessing `.id` or `.integration` directly, or checking truthiness where `[]` is truthy), the reminder calendar invite would be malformed or omitted.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: The body of sendOrganizerRequestReminderEmail and the CalEvent parser/email template handling of evt.destinationCalendar; this file is not in the visible related batches.

contracts: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar consumed by the reminder email path is now `DestinationCalendar[]` (possibly `[]`). Downstream email/calendar code must treat it as an array and tolerate empty arrays.
Selection fallback semantics are preserved for a single calendar: booking-level calendar wins over user-level calendar; otherwise empty.

investigations.question: Does an un-migrated caller still pass destinationCalendar as a single object (not an array)?
investigations.claim: createAllCalendarEvents() uses `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, which throws TypeError if destinationCalendar is a non-iterable object; also create()'s destructure could behave unexpectedly.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Caller evidence for handleConfirmation.ts and handleNewBooking.ts confirming destinationCalendar is always set as an array in this proposal.

contracts: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array; all callees iterate it.
EventResult.externalId is populated by createEvent; updateEvent's population is unverified.
create() must not throw when destinationCalendar is empty even if location is Google Meet.
createAllCalendarEvents() integrates each destination's externalId into the created reference.
updateAllCalendarEvents() returns one update result per calendar reference and one failure entry per reference on error.
CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now consumed as an array by collaborators (EventManager/CalendarService in related batches); index 0 is the organizer/eventType primary calendar.
Booking.destinationCalendar connect uses the first (primary) calendar; booking carry-over on createBooking uses evt.destinationCalendar[0].
loadUsers failure mode for empty dynamicUserList changed from downstream 'No available users found' to an immediate 500 'Unable to load users'.

investigations.question: Are all reads of CalendarEventClass.destinationCalendar outside the shown related-change batches (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts, EventManager.ts, types Calendar.d.ts) migrated to handle the array type? The class itself provides no single-object fallback; any unmigrated consumer doing property access or truthiness checks on the value would misbehave at runtime for array values.
investigations.claim: A consumer still treating destinationCalendar as a single DestinationCalendar could throw (property access on array) or select wrong behavior when multiple calendars exist.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Full set of consumers of CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar (other calendar apps, handlers, ics/outlook/office365/zoom paths) and confirmation each was updated in this PR; graph does not show REFERENCES to class.ts from those files.

investigations.question: Was CalendarEventBuilder.setDestinationCalendar (builder.ts:198-200) updated to emit an array into this field? It is not in the changed hunks; if it still assigns a single DestinationCalendar, its call sites would either fail type-checking or rely on a change elsewhere.
investigations.claim: Builder-produced CalendarEventClass instances may carry a stale single-object value if the builder path was not migrated, contradicting the array contract.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Source of CalendarEventBuilder.setDestinationCalendar and its callers to confirm array emission.

investigations.question: Does CalendarEvent (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) interface's destinationCalendar mirror the array type? The class implements CalendarEvent, so a mismatch (single in interface, array in class) would break implement/compile-time compatibility and any code typed against the interface.
investigations.claim: Interface/class type divergence would leave interface-typed consumers on the old single-object contract.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Updated declaration of destinationCalendar in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts (related batch-048f4bd85937642f).

contracts: createEvent callers must now pass a credentialId number.
Code consuming CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar must treat it as an array (or null), not a single object.
updateEvent/deleteEvent still accept an optional externalCalendarId; the new array lookup only honors it when a truthy string is passed.
createEvent insertion targets the calendar matching the given credentialId, falling back to primary when no match exists.

No contract changes. `Booking` is used only as a type (`buildRescheduleLink(booking: Partial<Booking>)`), so `import type` is valid. `Prisma` is used as a value (`Prisma.validator<Prisma.UserArgs>()` and `Prisma.UserGetPayload`), so it remains a runtime import; both symbols remain available in this module.

destinationCalendar on the CalendarEvent class (and per PR, the CalendarEvent interface / other call sites) now holds an array of destination calendars: consumers selecting the 'main' calendar must index (e.g., [0]) and iterate for multi-host invites; any read of object properties (primaryEmail/credentialId/... ) or truthiness-as-single-object semantics on this field now fails for array inputs.

The fallback behavior described by the PR (single main destinationCalendar still works, multiple supported) is implemented in consuming code (GoogleCalendarService, EventManager, types/Calendar.d.ts) in the same PR; this hunk provides no equivalent fallback on the class itself.

investigations.question: Is CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar consistently typed/migrated to an array at every call site that constructs CalendarEvent used by this email, given this component destructively iterates it with array destructuring?
investigations.claim: If any caller still supplies the old single object shape for destinationCalendar, array destructuring would throw 'object is not iterable' at runtime.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: The CalendarEvent type definition and each construction site of destinationCalendar (the PR states all usages were patched, which is counterevidence but not independently verified in the supplied source).

contracts: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array of destination calendar entries; consumers must treat it as iterable.
BrokenIntegrationEmail emits a calendar-name in the broken_calendar_action email text derived from `integration` field of the first entry by splitting on '_' and capitalizing the first two parts.
The email's literal 'calendar' fallback unchanged for missing/empty destinationCalendar.

investigations.question: Are there any remaining callers that still pass the old single-object destinationCalendar shape?
investigations.claim: Destructuring a non-array value would throw a TypeError (object not iterable), aborting event creation/listCalendars.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Full call graph of createEvent and listCalendars confirming all callers were migrated to the array type.

contracts: createEvent callers must now pass a credentialId number.
Code consuming CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar must treat it as an array (or null), not a single object.
updateEvent/deleteEvent still accept an optional externalCalendarId; the new array lookup only honors it when a truthy string is passed.
createEvent insertion targets the calendar matching the given credentialId, falling back to primary when no match exists.

createEvent: given a destinationCalendar array whose first element's externalId is absent from the service account's calendar list, zero events are created and a success result is returned (no exception, no error response).
listCalendars: IntegrationCalendar.primary reflects only the first destination calendar entry and can be false for valid user calendars or true for a calendar belonging to the main host only.
Both methods now assume event.destinationCalendar is iterable (array); callers must supply the new array type or destructuring will throw.

investigations.question: Are Prisma relations User.destinationCalendar and Booking.destinationCalendar single objects (DestinationCalendar?) or arrays (DestinationCalendar[])?
investigations.claim: If either field is already an array, wrapping it in a new array creates a nested array (e.g. [[cal1, cal2]]), which would break downstream calendar consumers that expect DestinationCalendar[].
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Prisma schema definitions or TypeScript types for User.destinationCalendar and Booking.destinationCalendar, plus the session/select that produced ctx.user and the booking select.

investigations.question: Do all consumers of evt.destinationCalendar in the confirmation/calendar-sending path handle both the new [] value and the array type correctly?
investigations.claim: Returning [] instead of null changes truthiness; a consumer that checks `if (evt.destinationCalendar)` may enter the calendar path with no actual calendar and fail when no destination calendar is configured.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: Implementation of handleConfirmation and calendar-message sending code that uses evt.destinationCalendar.

contracts: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now expected to be an array by this handler; evt passed to handleConfirmation will contain an array with zero or one destination calendar records.

When neither booking nor user has a destination calendar, the value changes from null/undefined to [], so consumers must treat an empty array as 'no destination calendar' rather than checking truthiness of destinationCalendar.

candidates.title: Crash in create() when destinationCalendar is an empty array
candidates.reason: The fallback check now destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `[]` (or undefined), the destructured element is `undefined` and `undefined.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The previous code used optional chaining `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and was safe for a missing calendar. The companion webhook edits (paypal-webhook.ts and webhook.ts) explicitly set `destinationCalendar: []` when neither the booking nor the user has a destination calendar, so a paid Google-Meet booking without any destination calendar reaches this crash during `eventManager.create(evt)`, preventing the booking reference creation and payment confirmation.
evidenceToCheck: Confirm the empty-array case is reachable: webhook callers pass destinationCalendar: [] when no calendar is set; verify no other guard prevents create() from running with location === MeetLocationType.

contracts: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array; all callees iterate it.
EventResult.externalId is populated by createEvent; updateEvent's population is unverified.
create() must not throw when destinationCalendar is empty even if location is Google Meet.
createAllCalendarEvents() integrates each destination's externalId into the created reference.
updateAllCalendarEvents() returns one update result per calendar reference and one failure entry per reference on error.
CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array (possibly empty or multi-element) that downstream consumers must tolerate; an empty array must be a valid value.
Consumers that previously read destinationCalendar?.X now must handle undefined first element plus possibly multiple entries.
PayPal webhook path depends on EventManager.create not throwing for bookings with Meet location and no destination calendar.
CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is always an array; first element is the main host destination calendar, empty array means no destination calendar.

Payment webhook builds evt with destinationCalendar:[] when no booking/user calendar exists and passes it to EventManager.create for already-ACCEPTED paid bookings and to handleConfirmation/sendScheduledEmails otherwise.
EventManager.create dereferences the first element of destinationCalendar in the Google Meet fallback, so an empty array is no longer a safe absence signal.

candidates.title: Organization slug no longer stored when team billing is disabled
candidates.reason: Before the change the two conditions were complementary: `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` produced `{ slug }` in the create data, and `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` produced `{ requestedSlug: slug }` in metadata. The change makes both branches keyed on the same `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition, so in an environment where team billing is disabled the organization is created with neither `slug` in the data nor `requestedSlug` in `metadata`. The `metadata` block still unconditionally sets `isOrganization: true` and `orgAutoAcceptEmail`, and nothing later in `createHandler` assigns a slug, so such a deployment creates organizations with a null slug and no pending requested slug. Org subdomains/URLs are derived from the slug, so the org is left without its resolving slug; billing-enabled deployments conversely now set both `slug` and `requestedSlug` for the same value, duplicating the intended pending-approval signal. The regression to the previously complementary logic is observable in ordinary self-hosted (non-billing) runs of this handler, e.g. `check === false` with `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` unset.
evidenceToCheck: Confirm `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` constant evaluation in this file and that no later step in `createHandler` (e.g. the check branch or post-creation update) assigns `slug` or consumes `requestedSlug` for the non-billing path.
Check consumers of `metadata.requestedSlug` to see whether billing-enabled orgs now setting both `slug` and `requestedSlug` breaks pending-approval/waitlist assignment logic.

investigations.question: Is there a post-creation routine (outside this unit) that assigns `slug` from `requestedSlug` or otherwise backfills the org slug in non-billing environments?
investigations.claim: If such a backfill exists, the missing-slug regression in non-billing deployments could be mitigated, changing the finding's severity.
investigations.evidenceNeeded: A caller or follow-up procedure that reads `metadata.requestedSlug` or sets `team.slug` after this handler returns in the `check === false` non-billing path.

contracts: The `organization.create` payload previously guaranteed exactly one of `slug`/`requestedSlug` depending on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`; it now guarantees none when billing is disabled and both when enabled. `metadata.isOrganization`, `isOrganizationVerified`, `isOrganizationConfigured` and `orgAutoAcceptEmail` remain unconditional.
